acceptance_criteria.S6B-M-AC-01: three fresh successful transitions each prove exact warmup/canary/switch/drain/unload/rollback phase and identity order from request, span, independent clock-anchor, and PostgreSQL durable-effect records
acceptance_criteria.S6B-M-AC-02: each fresh successful transition joins exactly 1,000 accepted requests to 1,000 terminal results and 1,000 unique committed/read-back durable effects with loss, duplicate, 5xx, retry, outcome-unknown, cross-version contamination, and illegal GPU owner overlap all zero
acceptance_criteria.S6B-M-AC-03: wrong-digest, load, readiness, canary, and VRAM guards each fail closed for repetitions 1, 2, and 3 while Blue remains the exact route and no terminal effect is created
acceptance_criteria.S6B-M-AC-04: frozen p99 and inter-completion-gap limits, exact Blue rollback, B0 CUDA health, Prometheus, model unload, PostgreSQL effect visibility, queue/lease state, and deterministic cleanup pass for every accepted repetition

claim_boundary: one Windows/WSL2 physical node, one RTX 4080, one Triton GPU container, one local PostgreSQL control-plane instance, controlled traffic; not production SLA, database HA/DR durability, physical HA, node failover, multi-node, multi-GPU, MIG, MPS, or a zero-interruption guarantee

clock_contract.hash_chain: sequence plus previous_anchor_hash plus source/process/host identity
clock_contract.projection: request monotonic timestamps are projected only through the run-level anchor envelope; OTLP, PostgreSQL, and phase Unix timestamps are never calibrated from a request span

definition: one top-level exclusive GPU lease and one Triton GPU container host governed Blue and Green model identities; the existing Workloads API controls warmup, canary, switch, long Blue drain, unload, rollback, and a real PostgreSQL terminal-effect commit before returning request success

durable_terminal_effect_contract.ack_order: Triton result and hold complete, then one PostgreSQL entity plus idempotency response commit with synchronous_commit=on, then independent transaction readback, then API success response
durable_terminal_effect_contract.canonical_timestamp: the commit interval is conservatively bounded by database clock_timestamp recorded inside the write transaction and clock_timestamp from an independent post-commit readback; controller_end is an auxiliary upper bound only
durable_terminal_effect_contract.identity: unique attempt_id/request_id/effect_id with offered and served role/name/version/artifact, result digest, generation, phase, trace identity, database transaction identity, and readback visibility
durable_terminal_effect_contract.repository: existing TransactionalControlPlaneStore entities and idempotency_keys tables in an isolated S6B-M schema
durable_terminal_effect_contract.replay: same request digest returns the same durable entity and creates no second effect

experiment_purpose: measure model lifecycle continuity and guard behavior while proving request completion against independently observable clocks and a canonical durable terminal effect
historical_evidence_policy: all V1/V2/V3 evidence and the first 104 ledger events remain immutable and receive no V4 acceptance credit

remediation_trigger.finding: Strict V3 derived a per-request clock offset from the same request completion and used controller_end as terminal effect; a coherent post-switch span-start mutation passed and no independent durable effect record existed

test_purpose: prove every old and new raw mutation fails closed, including coherent cross-clock and durable-effect attacks, while the positive fresh suite passes
validation_purpose: independently recompute request/span/phase/clock/effect identity, conservative ordering intervals, metric deltas, repetitions, fault guards, resources, and cleanup from immutable raw artifacts
